summary: I closed the seven obligations that validation and review sent back. None of them needed a design change. The context menu now sends 'Open in Explorer' to the window itself, using the row the app captured when the menu opened. So the entry stays enabled and works on a results-list row mid-scan, after a live refresh has detached that row's container. In the tests, the reveal hook now only observes the app and never fills in the row itself. R-001 gained a mid-scan step, a real placeholder-row step and a 'dup.' decoy check that can actually fail. The B-007/B-008 variants with the status line on screen now prove the line was there and one line tall. I ran R-001, B-007 and B-008 against the published exe and real Explorer, and all passed. The Core suite passed on a re-run: the first full run failed one Core cancel-timing test that this slice does not touch. A temporary broken build showed that the new mid-scan step fails on the old routing.

files.why: O-024/O-030: removed the MenuItem's CommandTarget binding to PlacementTarget and the Window-level ContextMenuOpening handler; the budget comment is corrected to the 644 px minimum (code-review drift about '396 px' at :155-172), with no layout change

O-024/O-030: OnRowContextMenuOpened is the only capture. It sets each MenuItem's CommandTarget to the Window and Tag to the row, or to a NoRow stand-in when the row is null or BindingOperations.DisconnectedSource, so the entry is disabled rather than acting on a stale or focused row. O-029: Failed, NoLongerExists and catch-block status texts now put the outcome first and the path last

O-026: the menu steps open the menu as ContextMenuService does, flush the dispatcher, then read and log whether the app captured the row, and never write menu.Tag. O-024: top-live opens a results-list row's menu mid-scan, waits until a live refresh detaches the container, forces a requery, logs enabled/open/detached/scanning, clicks the item and logs the reveal. O-026(b): the placeholder step draws a real placeholder container (the folder's Expanded is held back for one expansion) and opens its own RowContextMenu. O-028: WaitForTopRow runs before Stop
O-027: the 'drives in' line appends status=<visible> statusHeight=<px> when FSA_HOOK_STATUS is set; the header documents it

O-025: the non-baseline Explorer windows are closed, and waited out, before every R-001 step. 'dup.' runs before the root step, and the decoy check polls for 2 s. O-026: Invoke-RevealRun requires captured=true on every menu line, and the placeholder step requires found/captured/disabled. O-024: top-live asserts detached, scanning, open, enabled, the revealed path and the Explorer selection. O-027: CheckStatusShown is asserted in Invoke-StoppedEnding and in a new Completed-ending status variant in B-007

obligations.how: OnRowContextMenuOpened sets every MenuItem's CommandTarget to the Window, and the PlacementTarget binding at MainWindow.xaml:17 is gone. The row comes from the menu's Tag, captured when the menu opened. The new R-001 top-live step opens a TopLevelList row's menu mid-scan and waits until a live refresh has detached the container (logged sentinel=true, scanning=true). It then re-queries and asserts that the entry is still enabled and the menu still open, clicks it, and asserts an Exact reveal of that row with Explorer selecting it. This passed twice. A temporary build without the CommandTarget fix gave enabled=false and no reveal on the same step. The source was restored and republished, and R-001 passed again on the restored build.

Before every R-001 step, $closeNewWindows quits only the hwnds that were absent at the case's baseline, waits until they are gone and asserts that none are left. The 'dup.' step runs before the root step. It asserts that the ancestor 'reveal-root' is selected in a window that step opened, then polls the $root windows for 2 s and asserts that 'dup' is never selected. Passed.

(a) The hook no longer writes menu.Tag. It opens the menu (PlacementTarget, then IsOpen), flushes the dispatcher and logs 'captured' from the app's own Opened handler. Invoke-RevealRun requires captured=true on every menu line; all 19 were true. (b) The placeholder step draws a real placeholder row container by holding back the folder's Expanded for one expansion, then opens that container's own RowContextMenu. It logs found/captured/disabled, and R-001 requires all three to be true. Passed.

When FSA_HOOK_STATUS is set, the hook's 'drives in' line now ends with status=True statusHeight=15.96. CheckStatusShown asserts the line is visible and at most 24 px including its 6 px margin. It is called from Invoke-StoppedEnding whenever $statusMsg is given. B-007 gained a Completed-ending variant (expand mode, minimum size, 26 drives, status shown) that checks CheckBothLists with the folder tree. B-007 and B-008 passed.
In RevealMode, the 'top:' step now calls WaitForTopRow for the target name after the scan starts and before StopScan, as watch mode does. R-001's stopped-scan top step passed.

FormatRevealStatus's Failed and NoLongerExists texts, and the Failed text in OnOpenInExplorer's catch block, now put the outcome first and the path last: "Couldn't open Explorer: <msg> (0x<hr>). '<path>'" and "No longer exists, so highlighting '<shown>' instead: '<requested>'". The one-line trim therefore cuts the path, not the reason. No test asserts these strings.

The GetType().Name comparisons are gone. OnRowContextMenuOpened uses ReferenceEquals(row, BindingOperations.DisconnectedSource). In that case, or when the row is null, it stores a NoRow stand-in, which PathOf maps to an empty path, so the entry is disabled. The Window-level ContextMenuOpening handler is removed; Opened alone does the capture.

tests.note: First run: 295 passed, 1 failed. The failure was SynchronousIoCancelTests.CancelIsResentWhileACallBlocksAgainAfterACancel ('the call was still blocked 2 s after Cancel'), a Core timing test this slice does not touch; there is no Core change in the diff. Rerunning that class alone gave 25/25 and the full re-run below passed.

Ran twice, both PASSED: once on the new build, once after the source was restored and the app republished. It uses the real published exe and the real Explorer. Every step closed its Explorer windows first (0 left each time). top-live logged captured, detached, sentinel, scanning, enabled and open all true, with an Exact reveal of the row and Explorer selecting it. Placeholder: found, captured and disabled all true. 'dup.' landed on the ancestor, and the decoy was never selected during the 2 s poll.

The new Completed variant at 560x644 with the status line shown passed: status=True, statusHeight=15.96, and every list kept a full row (FolderTree 2 full rows). The Cancelled status variant also passed.
The status variant asserted status=True, statusHeight=15.96.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $env:TEMP/sl047-disc.ps1 (scratch, deleted) against a temporary build without CommandTarget, published to %TEMP%/sl047-broken (deleted)
tests.note: This shows the new test can fail. On the old routing, the top-live step logged enabled=false with an empty path and kind (no reveal), with captured/detached/sentinel/scanning/open all true. The fixed build gives enabled=true and an Exact reveal. The source was restored straight after the publish; the grep shows item.CommandTarget = this at MainWindow.xaml.cs:722.

This is the shipped exe started through its real entry point on real input (this repo's src folder, 1022 files and 64 folders). It exited 0 with 'Finished', and the folder tree was in view with 3 full rows.

tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-R001 ('dup.' ancestor landing and 2 s decoy poll)

deviations: R2-B4-2's fix said to keep the row when the sentinel is seen. Instead, when OnRowContextMenuOpened sees the disconnected sentinel or a null row, it stores a NoRow stand-in rather than leaving Tag alone. The StaticResource ContextMenu in each ItemContainerStyle is one instance shared by that list's rows, so leaving Tag alone would keep the row from an earlier opening, which is a silent wrong target. A null Tag would instead make the command fall back to the keyboard-focused row. NoRow disables the entry.
B3-1's fix allowed either the owning ItemsControl or the Window as CommandTarget. I chose the Window, because it holds the CommandBinding and no refresh can detach it.
follow_ups: Ctrl+Enter on a results-list row during a live scan: each refresh replaces the list's items, so the focused ListBoxItem goes away and Ctrl+Enter then finds no row. The entry is disabled, so it never acts on a wrong target, but it does nothing. Validation recorded this as not reached. It needs a design decision, such as keeping focus or selection across refreshes, which is SL-039 territory.

docs/design/SL-039-live-results.md:74 ('560 by 620 and up') and docs/design/SL-044-folder-tree.md:60 ('its minimum stays 620') describe the minimum height before SL-047 raised it to 644. They are those slices' own design records, so I left them unedited. A note, or an SL-047 design doc recording the change, would close the drift code-review raised.
The O-029 status wording is not asserted by any test. A Core-side formatter test would pin it, but FormatRevealStatus lives in the App, which has no unit-test project.
